entries.title: Proverbs 1 — Chapter Introduction
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Written - Appointed and declared in the holy scripture. Chapter 150 An exhortation to praise God with all sorts of musical instruments, ver. 1 - 6.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Written - Appointed and declared in the holy scripture. Chapter 150 An exhortation to praise God with all sorts of musical instruments, ver. 1 - 6.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To know - Written to help men to know throughly and practically. Both human wisdom to conduct our affairs in this life, and Divine wisdom. Instruction - The instructions delivered either by God, or men, in order to the attainment of wisdom. To perceive - Which teach a man true understanding.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To receive - Willing to receive the counsels of others. Such as makes men wise and prudent, and to teach just judgments or equity.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Simple - Such as want wisdom. Young man - Who wants both experience and self - government.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Will hear - Is willing to learn. Attain to - The art of governing himself or others.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The fear - Reverence and obedience to God. Beginning - The foundation without which all other knowledge is vain. Fools - That is, wicked men, are so far from attaining true wisdom, that they despise it, and all the means of getting it.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My son - He speaks to his scholars with paternal authority and affection. Of thy mother - Those pious instructions, which thy mother instilled into thee in thy tender years.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In vain - The fowler who spreads, his net in the sight of the bird looseth his labour. But these, are more foolish than the silly birds, and though they are not ignorant of the mischief which these evil courses will bring upon themselves, yet they will not take warning.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Their own blood - The destruction which they design to others, fall upon themselves.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Greedy - That seeks gain by wicked practices.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wisdom - Having expressed the counsels of wicked men, he now declares the voice of wisdom. By wisdom he understands the wisdom of God revealed to men in his word. And this is said to cry with a loud voice, to intimate God's earnestness in inviting sinners to repentance. Abroad - Or, in the streets or open places. Not in corners, but openly before all the world.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Gates - Where magistrates sit in judgment, and people are assembled. The city - Not only in the gate, but in every part of the city.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Scoffers - That scoff at religion and contemn the word and faithful ministers of God.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My words - By my spirit I will cause you to understand my word.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Called - By my ministers, by my judgments, and by the motions of my spirit and your own conscience.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Your fear - The misery you do or should fear.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:28
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Early - With diligence and fervency.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Knowledge - The practical knowledge of God and of their duty.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Eat - They should receive punishment answerable to their sins. Filled - With the fruits of them.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Turning - From God. Destroy - Shall prove the occasion of their ruin, by making them presumptuous, and secure.
